name: IvyForms – The innovative Contact Form Builder
author: wpDataTables

sections.description:
The Most innovative WordPress Contact Form Builder Plugin – Beta

IvyForms gives you innovative interface, easy customization, views, powerfully integrations and reporting.

More to come in the future releases, but for now you can use it to create simple contact forms.

Coming soon:
– New Templates
– More security features (Honeypot, etc.)
– Integrations with wpDataTables.
– New field types and more

External services

This plugin connects to the ipwho.is API to obtain country code information for phone number field localization. This feature helps improve user experience by auto-selecting the appropriate country code for phone input fields.

What data is sent:
– The plugin sends an IP address lookup request to ipwho.is when a form with a phone number field is loaded
– No personal identifying information is explicitly sent, but the user’s IP address is implicitly transmitted as part of the request

When data is sent:
– Only when forms with phone number functionality are loaded and used

This service is provided by “https://ipwhois.io”:
– Terms of service: https://ipwhois.io/terms
– Privacy policy: https://ipwhois.io/privacy
sections.installation:
Installation of the plugin is really simple.

  1. Install using one of these options:
    • Install directly from WordPress Admin panel: go to Plugins -> Add New -> Search for “IvyForms”, and click the Install button.
    • Download the ZIP manually from WordPress’ plugins repository, and upload it through WordPress Admin panel: go to Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin, browse to the downloaded Zip and upload it.
    • Download the ZIP, extract it and manually upload the extracted folder through FTP to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory of your WordPress installation.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to the IvyForms tab at the bottom of your admin menu and click the “Add New” button to begin creating your new WordPress contact form.
  4. That’s it!
sections.faq:
Who should use IvyForms?

IvyForms is perfect for business owners, bloggers, designers, developers, photographers, and basically everyone else. If you want to create a custom WordPress form, then you need to use the IvyForms drag & drop form builder.
sections.changelog:
0.4

  • Added Name field.
  • Added Radio Button field.
  • Added Address field.
  • Added Advanced Options (Max Length, Default Value, Field Label Position, No Duplicates) for relevant fields.
  • Added new general field settings for relevant fields.
  • Added Dynamic Placeholder Linking in Notification and Confirmation Settings.
  • Added option in Global Settings to enable WCAG-compliant backend.
  • Fixed issue with fatal error on activation due to DI\Container declaration conflict in WP 6.8.2.
  • Fixed issue with date filter not returning results for exact date selection.
  • Fixed issue with unsaved changes popup appearing despite saving.
  • Fixed issue with New Form popup overflowing on smaller screens.
  • Fixed drag and drop and field reorder errors.
  • Fixed various CSS-related issues to improve layout and styling consistency.
    Other small bug fixes and stability improvements.

0.3.1

  • Added Website field.
  • Added new general field settings including Hide Label, Read Only, Description, Required Message, CSS Classes.
  • Fixed issue with reload on Confirmation tab causing warning popup to appear.
  • Fixed various CSS-related issues to improve layout and styling consistency.
  • Fixed issue with delayed tab switching due to prolonged success message after form save.
  • Fixed issue with confirmation messages generated using form id instead of confirmation id.
  • Fixed issue with reload on Confirmation tab causing warning popup to appear.
  • Fixed issue with creating a new form from template causing error.

0.3

  • Implemented reCaptcha integration for security.
  • New Admin page for Settings and reCaptcha configuration.
  • Added logic for storing Form Submissions as Entries in the database.
  • New Admin page for listing and handling Form Entries.
  • New Results tab in the Form Builder page for displaying the Entries of the Form.
  • Added option to enable/disable Entry storage of a single Form in the database.
  • Added Entry Details view in the Admin to see individual submission data
  • Added a new Form creation step – Picking from Templates or starting from scratch
  • Create a Contact Form using template for quick form creation
    Other small bug fixes and stability improvements.

0.2.1

  • Implemented scrollbar variations and consistent pagination across tables.
  • Added loader to Save button and matched its size with Update button.
  • Added support icon to the header for quicker help access.
  • Fixed issue with form preview not working when plugin is installed in a subfolder.
  • Fixed issue with Settings page breaking after editing Confirmation tab.
  • Fixed issue with “Rows per page” after table action on All Forms Page.
  • Fixed issue with sorting after All Forms table actions.
  • Fixed inconsistent filter indicator behavior.
    Other small bug fixes and stability improvements.

0.2

  • Full WCAG compliance across all frontend elements.
  • Added the option to publish or unpublish each form from its settings.
  • Enhanced search logic in the Notification table.
  • Improved filters on the All Forms table.
  • “Redirect to page” dropdown now shows the page name instead of the ID.
  • Fixed a drag-and-drop issue in the Form Builder.
  • Fixed an issue with duplicated forms.
  • General UI/UX improvements (tooltips, sticky buttons, pagination behavior, scroll styling, etc.).
  • CSS fixes.
  • Compatibility with WordPress version 6.8.2 approved.
    Other small bug fixes and stability improvements.

0.1.2

  • Initial MVP ( minimum viable product ) release
